⛔⛔ CAUGHT A REAL, ALREADY-PUSHED DEFECT ON main, INTRODUCED BY THIS SESSION TWO CYCLES AGO: running PREFLIGHT_TESTS=1 (the first time this session ran it since CYC-0036) failed test_the_manifest_revision_is_a_commit_a_reader_can_resolve — the archive manifest committed in CYC-0036 (b389f3c14, currently on origin/main) records git_revision a23fa5c366..., which is NOT reachable on any branch or tag. Root cause, confirmed rather than guessed: CYC-0036 regenerated the manifest, then a push was rejected by a concurrent CI commit, forcing a rebase that rewrote a23fa5c36 to ea83fc145 — and this session explicitly chose NOT to re-regenerate the manifest a second time afterward (reasoning at the time: '--check-archive still passes, so this is just cosmetic', which was WRONG — --check-archive verifies the file inventory, not whether git_revision is a resolvable commit, and a dedicated separate test exists precisely for that second question, which this session did not run before pushing because PREFLIGHT_TESTS was skipped on that push). CYC-0034 hit the identical rebase situation and DID correctly re-regenerate a second time (commit 1468c7a9d, 're-regenerate ASO archive manifest after rebase') — CYC-0036 was the one place this session got complacent. Fixed in this cycle: manifest regenerated against the final, post-merge, pre-push tree, and (per the lesson) will be regenerated AGAIN after any further rebase this push needs, not skipped.
Archive manifest regenerated as an isolated follow-up commit per its own ordering requirement, AND verified this time with the dedicated resolvability test, not just --check-archive.
what_i_got_wrong: CYC-0036 regenerated the archive manifest after a rebase-forced push rejection, checked only `--check-archive` (the file-inventory question), and explicitly decided the `git_revision` staleness this caused was cosmetic/human-only. It was not: a dedicated test (test_the_manifest_revision_is_a_commit_a_reader_can_resolve.py) exists specifically to catch a git_revision left dangling by a post-regeneration rebase, and it went unrun on that push because PREFLIGHT_TESTS=1 was not set for it. The defect sat on origin/main for two cycles before this one's PREFLIGHT_TESTS=1 run caught it. Lesson, stated plainly: '--check-archive passes' is not the same claim as 'the manifest's provenance line is sound after a rebase' — the two are different tests for different questions, and CYC-0034's own handling of the identical situation (re-regenerate a second time, unconditionally, after any rebase) was the correct instinct that CYC-0036 abandoned under a false economy.
